messages:
ops-oncall: FYI customer (AcmeCorp) reporting mass 502s and timeouts against hosted inference in az1 ~12:22 UTC. Multiple 503/502 spikes and auth token validation failures. Can we triage?

maria: Seeing a spike in 5xx for model/generate on az1 from our gateway metrics. Error ratio ~18% over 3m. Latency p50 doubled.

chen: Logs show a lot of upstream reset/errors from edge-gw -> backend pool, plus repeated `502 gateway_error` with `read tcp: connection reset by peer`.

sam: Customer says they also saw billing errors in their dashboard when requests retried, raised a support ticket. Tagging @support-bot to pull the ticket thread.

support-bot: Ticket #13587 linked: "AcmeCorp: sustained 502s in region az1, observed token failures and duplicate charges on retry". CC: CS.

netops: I'm seeing packet loss and intermittent retransmits on the az1 interconnect to provider-2 around 12:20-12:26 UTC: loss ~3-4% and microbursts. Provider reports BGP flap on peer ASN 64513 at timestamp 2024-11-15T12:21:xxZ.

maria: That matches our internal telemetry: cross-zone KV cache misses spiked (prefix cache warmups) and backend auth timeouts at auth-service (timeouts increased from 200ms -> 2s).

chen: Repro steps from an internal curl: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate` shows `HTTP/2 502` and `upstream read timeout`. Pasted snippet:
```
* Connected to api.redwood.ai (10.0.1.5) port 443
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/2
< HTTP/2 502
< content-type: application/json
{
  "error": {"type":"gateway_error","message":"upstream read timeout"}
}
```

sam: Temporary mitigation proposal: enable route fallback from az1 -> az2 for hosted inference traffic and spin up extra edge proxies in az2. Also enable our model-variant fallback to smaller quantized model to reduce backend load.

netops: I'm already asking provider-2 for route dampening and to keep the session open. Pushing an immediate ebgp-graceful-restart request. If provider can't stabilize, we'll failover egress to provider-1.

maria: Can infra/eng-runtime also temporarily increase auth-service deadline to 5s and accept longer token validation latencies? That will reduce 5xx surface.

chen: Changing auth deadline now on the canary path: `auth.timeout=5000ms` on auth-svc canary. Rolling to 10% first.

billing: On the billing side — AcmeCorp reported duplicate billing for retried requests. We need to check idempotency keys and coordinate credits if confirmed. I can pre-authorize a credit until we confirm counts.

support-bot: Customer updated ticket: "We're getting 502s in az1 since 12:20, traffic critical for SLAs, please update". They asked for ETA.

ops-oncall: Standup: @netops escalate to provider on call, @chen @maria track metrics and share graph snapshots, @billing prepare provisional credit, @customer-success get bridge + runbook with customer. Set bridge in 10m.

customer-success: Joining bridge with AcmeCorp now, collecting repro manifests and sample request ids. Asking them to switch region to az2 for immediate relief (we have a fallback guide).

netops: Provider acknowledged flap and applied route dampening at 12:33; observed packet loss trend falling to ~0.5% by 12:38. We're failing over a subset of traffic to provider-1 as a precaution.

maria: Metrics: 5xx dropped to baseline over next 7m after auth timeout bump + partial failover. p95 latency back to normal by 12:46.

ops-oncall: Resolution summary: root cause = provider-2 BGP flap causing interconnect microbursts and upstream TCP resets -> auth timeouts -> 502s. Mitigation = temporary auth deadline bump, partial egress failover to provider-1, enable az1->az2 route fallback, customer region guidance + provisional billing credit.

billing: Will issue provisional credit and follow up once logs confirm duplicate charge volume.

ops-oncall: Closing thread after postmortem. Will open follow-up to review more aggressive automatic failover and idempotency checks. :white_check_mark:
